passage: Ramesh's birthday get-together was set for Sunday, and everyone kept asking why his father would not be there. He mumbled that Papa was travelling. His stomach twisted; he had told nobody about the separation, and he felt ashamed, as if something were wrong with his family. On Saturday rain cancelled cricket, and the boys crowded onto the verandah, noisy and curious. Ramesh looked at Yamini, who had been his friend since Class 2 and never spread stories. He took a breath. "My parents live in separate homes now. Please don't tell anyone yet." Yamini nodded. "Thanks for telling me. Some kids in my building have the same." Ramesh felt a little lighter.

qa.q: How long had Yamini been Ramesh's friend?
qa.a: Yamini had been his friend since Class 2.

qa.q: Why did Ramesh say Papa was travelling?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and did not want his friends to know about the separation.

qa.q: What was wise about how Ramesh chose who to tell?
qa.a: He chose one trusted friend who never spread stories, and asked Yamini to keep it private.

qa.q: How might Yamini see Ramesh telling her?
qa.a: Yamini probably felt trusted and wanted to comfort him, as her thanks and her remark about other kids in her building show.

grounding: A child ashamed of his parents' separation hides it, then confides in one trusted friend.

passage:
I'm Nilesh, and when my parents separated in Class 6, I told no one. When friends asked why my dad didn't come to sports day, I said he was busy.
Every lie made my stomach tight. I was sure everyone would think our family was broken.
Then one day Leela, who sat next to me, said her parents had separated two years earlier. She said it so simply.
After school I walked with her and told her everything. She just nodded. "It gets less weird."
I didn't tell the whole class. Just Leela. But for the first time in months, I didn't feel like I was hiding.

qa.q: What did Nilesh say when friends asked why Dad didn't come to sports day?

qa.a: Nilesh felt ashamed and afraid that everyone would think the family was broken.

qa.q: Why was telling Leela a good choice?
qa.a: Leela had been through the same thing and was kind, so sharing with one trusted friend ended the lonely feeling of hiding.

qa.q: How might Leela feel when Nilesh tells her?
qa.a: Leela may feel understanding and glad to help, since she had been through it herself.

grounding: Nilesh hides a parents' separation out of shame, then chooses one trusted friend to tell and feels less alone.

passage:
Note from the class teacher, Thursday.
Vaibhav has been quiet and edgy since the start of term. When the class made Father's Day cards, he said he'd "lost his pencil" and sat looking out of the window. I later learned from his mother that his parents have separated.
Today I noticed him talking quietly with Joseph at the back of the class during break. Joseph just nodded and listened. Vaibhav looked lighter afterwards and joined in the cricket match.
I spoke to Vaibhav briefly after school and told him he could always talk to me as well. He didn't say much, but he smiled.

qa.q: What did the class make that Vaibhav avoided?
How had Vaibhav seemed since the start of term?
qa.a: He seemed quiet, edgy and embarrassed, avoiding anything that might reveal his parents' separation.

qa.q: What helped Vaibhav start to feel lighter?
qa.a: Telling one trusted friend, Joseph, who listened, and knowing the teacher was also there to talk to.

qa.q: How might Joseph see his role in helping Vaibhav?
qa.a: Joseph seems to understand that listening quietly was enough, without making it a big deal.

grounding: A boy hides his parents' separation out of embarrassment, then tells one trusted friend and feels lighter.
